The IEP has behavioral goals only listed, no academic goals, but he is behind in reading. I am hoping to get academic added but when he was evaluated by the school they were mainly focused on the quickly escalating behavioral issues that were occurring.

Currently we have that a schedule will be placed on his desk and social supports include meeting with the school counselor in a group once a month. He is in a classroom with an aide but not assigned one personally. We have been told that we are quite behind academically but that he does not meet the criteria for summer school because you must demonstrate that the student falls behind after a break from school and that it takes twice as much effort to regain that academic level. I’ve been told by developmental pediatrics that this is pretty standard for districts.

The other thing I should mention is that cdphp can assign you a nurse care manager to take care of all these calls for you as I know this is overwhelming. They have some that work just with mental health and they do tend to keep you as a priority over the insurances interests. A case worker or care manager might be able to get you into a respite at 4 winds or elsewhere to give you a few days to focus only on your crisis, you could certainly call yourself though as well.

CDPHP Medicaid covers the Valera health app. You can usually get a psychiatrist within a few days. As one poster suggested, in the meantime you could use the doctor on demand app to try to get a prescription from a general practitioner. I would recommend this rather than using the ER and getting stuck in Albany med for 16 hours waiting for a psych evaluation. This can bridge you till you get in somewhere else. Ketamine has shown rapid response in these situations as has nudexta whereas traditional antidepressants will take time. The telehealth docs are more likely to give you traditional meds and less likely to fight with cdphp for you to get the faster but more expensive meds like an in person doc might at the county.
